rationale: Joint continuation on the two Qwen3ForCausalLM module groups of selection.json (prefill group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a, decode group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9). On this revision (2a42b9b1, new device) search.json installed_bundles is empty, so the current parent at both boundaries is the raw eager forward; nothing below is replaced (replaces stays empty). REPAIRED CONCRETE FAILURE: previous-feedback.txt records that trial trial-recovered-4f3d7f11aa installed correctly but its fast path was disabled at installation by its own gate - observations/previous-after/candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6.json shows _check_logits raising 'decode logits mismatch (eager_vs_parent_step_1)' at candidate line 877 - so all 62 decode calls routed parent_fallback_setup_failure and the run was a passthrough (decision reason fixed_diagnostic_only_fast_path_disabled). Cause: that trial's decode interior replaced the parent's heavy ops with custom kernels (Triton GEMV and a hand-written online-softmax attention without the parent's bf16 P rounding), whose reduction/rounding classes differ from cuBLAS gemvx and the flash splitkv SDPA kernel; the deviation exceeded its 0.008 gate at the very first step. Repair in this attempt: the decode interior keeps the parent's exact heavy computation - every projection is the same cuBLAS F.linear call on the same weights/shapes (bitwise identical op), and attention is the same F.scaled_dot_product_attention call with the same (1,32,1,128)x(1,8,seq,128) bf16 operands, scale=head_dim**-0.5, is_causal=False, enable_gqa=True that transformers 5.16.1 sdpa_attention_forward issues for q_len=1 (verified in the worker's installed source) - so only memory-layout ordering and launch structure change. What is fused/rewritten: (a) preallocated position-indexed K/V masters (1,8,287,128 bf16 per layer) written in place at the step position by one Triton kernel that also applies q_norm/k_norm and RoPE with the module's own bitwise-identical bf16 cos/sin table, removing the 72 CatArrayBatchedCopy concatenations plus feeding copies per step; (b) single-kernel RMSNorm and SiLU*up fusions replicating every eager bf16 rounding point (only fp32 reduction order of the variance sum and libdevice exp/rsqrt ulps can differ); (c) 31 per-step CUDA graphs over a shared pool, removing the host dispatch that dominates this device's eager decode. MEASURED FACTS motivating the graph/fusion work on this exact revision: the run is host-bound, not GPU-saturated - project_measurement baseline end_to_end_ms 701.76 / decode_ms 677.28 with decode diagnostic CUDA only 372.57ms (groups.json 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f), i.e. ~305ms of GPU idle from Python dispatch (python_runtime: ~27ms/step host across 145 RMSNorm forwards, 8096 linears, 4641 cats at ~2,073 kernels/step in call-resources); GPU decode splits into ~281.5ms cuBLAS gemvx (kept verbatim), ~10.7ms flash splitkv (kept verbatim) and ~80ms eagerly-decomposed tail (fused). EXPECTED EFFECT, to be tested by the framework's paired measurement and not assumed: decode wall approaches its GPU-bound floor, roughly 305-330ms in the fused configuration (end_to_end ~0.33-0.36s vs 0.70s baseline) or ~365ms in the exact fallback configuration; ttft is a pure passthrough to the parent prefill (previous passthrough measured ttft 23.55ms on this device class vs the 24.45ms 1.05x fresh-original-baseline limit), unchanged math and KV state. TWO-MODE BUILD CONVERTING FAILURE INTO SPEEDUP, NOT REJECTION: mode 'fused' (Triton fusions + parent GEMV/SDPA) is built first and gated; if any gate fails, the graphs are torn down and mode 'exact' is rebuilt - the same graph/masters structure but the interior is the parent's own module decomposition (layer.input_layernorm, q/k/v/o/gate/up/down nn.Linear, transformers apply_rotary_pos_emb on the same table, torch SiLU, torch residual adds, same SDPA), which reproduces the parent op sequence verbatim inside the graphs, so its deviation is at the fp32-reduction-order class of nothing (no custom numeric kernel at all). Gates in both modes, on the real GPU at build: per step, exact greedy-token equality plus logits assert_close vs the parent oracle chain at atol/rtol 0.012/0.012 (1.67x tighter than the required 0.02/0.02, and deliberately measuring the same quantity the quality check measures - fast-run vs parent-teacher-replay logits), bitwise equality between graph replay and eager execution of the same interior (one retry), final K/V state vs the oracle cache; then chain A (greedy through the installed replacements), chain B (rolled teacher-forced contiguous tokens through the fast path) vs chain C (the observe-time pattern itself: strided-(32,1) teacher slices threaded through the installed decode replacement, which routes to the parent exactly as adapter.observe will), chain D (repeated greedy invocation for continuity) and chain E (foreign-cache absorb). Any failure of both modes only disables the fast path while build() still returns exactly the two declared sites routing to the parent with the retained concise categories (parent_fallback_setup_failure, parent_fallback_signature, parent_fallback_replay_failure, prefill_parent_passthrough) - repairing both prior failure modes: the trial-45c44c1619 AttributeError-class crash (structural lookups now fail into _SetupFailure categories, rotary resolved on Qwen3Model per transformers 5.16.1) and the empty-install ValueError. eliminated_calls is empty: no separately-required observed call is dropped; the eliminated inner work (DynamicCache concatenation, eager norm/rope/silu decomposition kernels) is subsumed inside the replaced module boundary and the framework recaptures the plan from actual runtime evidence. Nothing fixture-dependent is captured: prefill runs the parent on the current input each invocation, the first decode call re-derives the masters from the cache it is actually given (content-based per-layer data_ptr ownership, absorb-by-refresh of any foreign cache), and each graph re-reads the static input token buffer (proven by the rolled-teacher chain B).
setup_work: All at installation (build) time on the leased worker, under torch.inference_mode(False) so persistent buffers are normal tensors (mutable later inside the adapter's inference-mode runs). (1) Structural extraction/validation of the Qwen3 module tree against transformers 5.16.1 (weights read in place, no copies or mutations; lm_head tied to the embedding). (2) One rotary_emb call producing the (287,128) bf16 cos/sin tables (~0.15 MB). (3) One real parent prefill to obtain the template cache and seed the masters. (4) Retained allocations for the worker lifetime: K/V masters 36x2x(1,8,287,128) bf16 = ~42.3 MB, 31 static logits buffers + scratch (1,1,151936) bf16 = ~10.0 MB, static (1,1) int64 token buffer, cos/sin ~0.15 MB, and one CUDA-graph pool holding per-step intermediates and SDPA/cuBLAS workspaces (~1-3 MB in fused mode; of order tens of MB in exact mode, sized by one step's eager intermediates and reused across the 31 graphs). Setup therefore raises framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated/reserved and the per-invocation allocated baseline by roughly 55-65 MB (fused) or ~90-140 MB (exact); per-invocation peak_allocated otherwise changes only by the first-call master refresh (~42 MB of copies once per invocation) and the per-step 0.3 MB logits clones - these are allocator/counter statements, not claims of general physical-memory savings, and no non-PyTorch driver allocation is involved. (5) 31 decode-graph captures (per-step eager warmup on the capture stream, capture, replay, bitwise compare against the eager execution) plus verification chains: oracle parent chain, greedy chain A, rolled teacher chain B, strided teacher pattern chain C, repeat greedy chain D, foreign-cache absorb chain E - each ~one extra generation unit of GPU work at installation, none of it part of the measured unit and none reused as cached output. (6) If the fused mode fails a gate, the graphs are torn down and rebuilt in exact mode (parent's own op decomposition), repeating the same allocations via the caching allocator; total installation is dominated by ~3-4 extra generation units plus Triton compilation of 3 small kernels, well inside the worker timeout.
quality_risks: Fused-mode numeric deviation vs the eager parent is restricted to fp32 reduction order in the RMSNorm variance sums (hidden 2560 and per-head 128) and libdevice exp/rsqrt ulps in SiLU/RoPE, since every projection is the parent's own cuBLAS F.linear and attention is the parent's own SDPA call on identically-shaped operands; expected logits deviation is far below the fused gate. The build gates measure the actual acceptance quantity (fast-run vs parent logits, all 32 steps x 151936 elements) at 0.012/0.012, 1.67x tighter than the required 0.02/0.02, and any failure automatically rebuilds in exact mode, whose interior is the parent's own module/op sequence captured verbatim.

Exact greedy-token requirement (torch.equal on all 32 positions): each step's token is gate-checked for equality against the parent oracle and the full chains A/D enforce chain-level equality; a top-2 margin below the residual deviation would fail the gate and degrade to exact mode or parent routing - lost speedup, never silently wrong tokens.

Observe-time teacher-forced replay enters through the installed decode replacement with stride-(32,1) slices; this is exactly the framework's signature-fallback path and is replicated at build (chain C threads those slices through the replacement into the parent, chain B compares the fast path on the same teacher tokens at 0.012/0.012, chain E validates foreign-cache absorb). Mirror caches are freshly built per call from a pristine template and the masters are re-derived from the cache actually passed, so no state leaks across invocations.

CUDA graph capture, cuBLAS/SDPA capture or Triton compilation failure, or an unexpected model structure: every failure path is a concise _SetupFailure category that only disables the fast path while build() still installs both declared sites routing to the parent (repair of both the trial-45c44c1619 AttributeError install crash and the empty-install ValueError that rejected trial-45c44c1619's first form).

CUDA Graph replay does not rerun Python hooks: the observed module site itself is invoked per step (the prior diagnostic counted 62 decode and 2 prefill replacement calls), and the graph interior is verified at build by bitwise replay-vs-eager comparison plus the per-step parent gates; route labels (fast_graph_replay, fast_graph_replay_refreshed, parent_fallback_*) remain diagnostic self-report only, never a substitute for the output checks.

If both modes fail their gates the candidate is a pure passthrough at eager-parent speed (~675-700 ms end_to_end on this device) - correct, constraint-satisfying, but without gain; the failure reason is retained in the runner's disable_reason for worker-side diagnostics.

Memory reporting: retained graph pools and masters raise lifecycle and per-run allocated counters as described in setup_work; peak_allocated counters falling or rising with capture-pool reuse is an allocator effect, not evidence of physical-memory savings or cost beyond the stated figures.
